study.title: Functional connectivity changes in the thalamocortical network due to neck pain and the multiscale regulatory effects of acupuncture: a cross-scale multi-omics neuroimaging study
study.blinding: patients, outcome assessors, data collectors, and statisticians remained blinded to group assignment
study.population: neck pain patients recruited from Shanxi University of Chinese Medicine and Shanxi Hospital of Acupuncture and Moxibustion
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) mechanical neck pain diagnosis; (2) VAS score >3 (0–10 range); (3) age 18–60 years; (4) right-handedness; (5) written informed consent
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) pregnancy/lactation; (2) communication-impairing psychiatric/neurological disorders; (3) MRI contraindications (e.g., claustrophobia, metallic implants); (4) concurrent clinical trial participation

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needle inserted at a shallow oblique angle of 15° to a depth of 2–3 mm. This depth reaches only the superficial skin layers (epidermis/dermis), engaging cutaneous Aβ/Aδ fibers but not reaching muscle or deep fascia. Falls within the 1–5 mm superficial penetration range (Level 2).

conditions.scan_context: resting-state fMRI; eyes closed, no head movement
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Identical insertion parameters to SA_pre: oblique angle of 15° to a depth of 2–3 mm. This constitutes superficial skin-only penetration (1–5 mm range), activating only cutaneous fibers without reaching muscle or deep fascia. Level 2 classification applies.

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Verum acupuncture at cervical tender points (lowest PPT sites)
acupoints_used_exact: four sites with lowest PPT values selected as acupuncture points; five body regions with the highest frequency of pain and the greatest acupoint sensitivity were selected for PPT detection; specific acupoint names not reported
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: cervical tender points; four sites with the lowest pressure pain threshold (PPT) values selected from five body regions
interventions.manipulation_exact: rotational manipulation (180° amplitude, 2 Hz frequency) for 1 min to elicit deqi sensation; manual stimulation reapplied for 1 min at 10-min intervals using identical manipulation parameters
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; deqi sensation (characteristic needling sensation) intended
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: licensed acupuncturists with at least 3 years of experience in acupuncture who completed standardized clinical trial protocol training
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: based on classic TCM principle of 'taking pain as the acupoint (Yi Tong Wei Shu)'; tender points represent pain-sensitized loci of cervical myofascial injury; PPT measured using digital algometer (Model FPX25), probe applied perpendicular to skin, pressure at constant rate of 1 kg/cm2/s until subject reported pain

extraction_notes.note: No deqi quantification instrument (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) was used or reported. The paper only states that deqi was intended in the VA group and not intended in the SA group. No quantitative deqi scores are available for extraction.
No expectancy, credibility, or blinding success measures (e.g., credibility/expectancy questionnaire, allocation guess rates) are reported anywhere in the paper.
No adverse events section is included in the paper. No statement about the presence or absence of adverse events was identified.

The between-group comparison for VAS is reported as Z = −6.877, p < 0.001, suggesting a non-parametric test (Mann-Whitney U or Wilcoxon rank-sum). The exact test name is not explicitly stated in the results section but is inferred from the Z statistic. The statistical test label in the extraction preserves the statistic as reported.

The paper states 'two-sample t-tests were conducted on the FC values of the subjects using the SPM12 software' for the neuroimaging analysis. This appears to be used as a within-group paired comparison (post vs. pre) rather than a between-group test, which is an atypical use of two-sample t-tests. The exact model specification is not further clarified in the methods.
The depth_mm_numeric for VA group is not precisely reported; the paper states 'depth adjusted per anatomical site' without providing numeric values. The field was left null.

The number of acupoints used per session in the VA group is stated as four (the four sites with lowest PPT values), but the specific anatomical region names and acupoint codes are not reported; only the selection method (pressure pain threshold) is described.

The PLS analysis was conducted on left hemisphere data only (58 brain regions × 15,633 genes) from AHBA. The paper states this limitation explicitly. The spatial correlation result (r = 0.445, Pspin = 0.0011) applies only to left hemisphere regions.
The paper references Supplementary Data 1 containing the full lists of PLS2+ (809 genes) and PLS2- (1,222 genes). These data were not available in the provided PDF and were not extracted.

The cluster extent unit for the neuroimaging results in Table 3 is labelled 'Cluster size' without specifying whether units are voxels or mm3. Extracted as 'voxels' based on typical SPM reporting convention, but this is an inference.

The paper reports 'five body regions with the highest frequency of pain and the greatest acupoint sensitivity were selected for PPT detection' but does not name these five body regions explicitly. Specific traditional acupoint names or codes are not provided for the VA group.

The specific resting-state fMRI scan duration in minutes is not explicitly stated; only '240 time points' with TR 2,000 ms is reported, implying approximately 8 minutes but this was not computed in the extraction.

The paper states that GO enrichment analysis identified 809 PLS2+ genes and 1,222 PLS2- genes. The exact gene lists are in Supplementary Data 1, which was not provided. Only the top-ranked genes visible in Figure 3e (ZNF189, GGTLC1, ARHGDIB, LPL, CD53 for positive; RPL13P5, LRP8, MGAT4C, SULF1, MCC for negative) could be read from the PDF.

The depth_mm_numeric for the sham acupuncture group was set to 2.5 as the midpoint of the reported range '2–3 mm'. This is an arithmetic midpoint, not a value explicitly stated in the paper. Users should note the reported range is 2–3 mm.

No between-group neuroimaging contrast (VA vs. SA direct comparison) is reported. All neuroimaging results are within-group pre-post comparisons. No between-group neuroimaging statistical maps or coordinates are available.

Session duration for the acupuncture procedure (beyond the 30-minute needle retention time) is not reported. It is unclear whether preparation, deqi induction, and post-needle time are included in a total session duration figure.
